key_concept: When the digit to be dropped is exactly $5$, the preceding digit stays the same if it is even and goes up by $1$ if it is odd (round-half-to-even rule).
steps: We keep three digits after the decimal point, so in each number the fourth decimal digit is dropped. In both numbers that digit is $5$.

Rule: if the dropped digit is greater than $5$, increase the preceding digit by $1$. If it is less than $5$, leave the preceding digit unchanged. If it is exactly $5$, leave the preceding digit unchanged when it is even and increase it by $1$ when it is odd.
For $17.0145$: the digit before the $5$ is $4$, which is even, so it stays. Result: $17.0145 \rightarrow 17.014$.
For $21.0235$: the digit before the $5$ is $3$, which is odd, so it becomes $4$. Result: $21.0235 \rightarrow 21.024$.
The rounded numbers are $17.014$ and $21.024$, which is option (3).
why_not_others: Option (4) comes from always rounding a $5$ upward, which ignores the even/odd rule for $17.0145$. Options (1) and (2) mishandle $21.0235$: its preceding digit $3$ is odd, so it must be raised to $4$.
common_trap: Applying the everyday 'always round $5$ up' habit, which gives $17.015$ and $21.024$ (option 4) instead of using the even/odd rule for a dropped $5$.
time_saving_tip: When the dropped digit is $5$, just check whether the digit before it is even (keep it) or odd (add $1$). Here $4 \rightarrow 4$ and $3 \rightarrow 4$, so pick option (3) directly.
